Thanks again for the demo today — the Scarlet team appreciated the clarity on cost controls and batch/reranker options. A few follow-ups from our infra side so we can scope the onramp work: 

- We want a VPC endpoint/private onramp so traffic from our prod cluster never traverses the public internet. What's your recommended pattern (VPC endpoint vs peering + NAT)?

- DNS & TLS: can we point a private CNAME to Redwood or do you require specific DNS delegation?
- mTLS: can Redwood accept client mTLS certs for authentication? If so, what format and rotation cadence do you support?
- SDK/auth: we plan to use server-side SDK calls with structured outputs / tool-calling and embeddings+reranker workflows. Any gotchas for SDK setup (OIDC vs API keys) when using private connectivity?

I've attached a quick network diagram and a short list of our security questions for SOC/Procurement. Can you confirm an initial list of docs and the engineers you want on the kickoff? We're aiming to start the onramp in the week of Apr 19.

Tom —

Great questions, thanks for the clear diagram. Below is a concise post-call recap with recommended architecture, owners, and next steps so we can get the onramp scheduled. I copied Karthik for the low-level auth and mTLS details. Ben will lead the commercial/contract side.

Summary of recommended approach (short):
- Connectivity pattern: Use a Redwood VPC Endpoint (Private Connect) into our Private Control Plane + a dedicated egress path for model inference. This avoids public egress IP allowlisting and simplifies DNS.
- IPs & allowlist: For control-plane and observability we will provide stable VIPs; inference egress is via the private path so you do not need to maintain a large public IP allowlist.
- DNS: We support either a private CNAME into our internal zone or a customer-managed private DNS resolver that maps your service name to the endpoint. We will share the DNS validation steps.
- mTLS & auth: We support client mTLS for the inference endpoint. You can present a client cert (PEM) issued by your PKI or use our short‑lived cert issuance flow. Rotation is supported via ACME-like renewal or an automated CA integration — we recommend quarterly rotation for long-lived certs, shorter for high‑security teams.
- SDK & auth flow: Server-to-server SDK calls are simplest with short-lived OIDC tokens minted by your IdP (recommended) or long-lived API keys if you need a quick proof-of-concept. Structured output / tool-calling works identically over the private path — the SDK includes a structured-output flag and JSON schema enforcement so you get validated payloads back.
- Embeddings + reranker: We recommend pushing embeddings from your vector pipeline directly to a private ingest endpoint (we provide S3-compatible signed uploads over private connectivity) and configuring our reranker as a local route to limit cross-region calls.

Deliverables we will provide by Apr 14:
1) Private connectivity checklist + IPs (redwood-integration-checklist.pdf) — owner: Olga Petrov
2) mTLS and cert rotation guidance (mTLS-cert-rotation-guidance.txt) — owner: Karthik Iyer
3) SDK quickstart for private onramp + example structured output schema — owner: Olga Petrov
4) HubSpot deal record and kickoff invite — owner: Ben Carter

Questions for Scarlet (please confirm):
- Which team will own the private DNS resolver (netops or platform)?
- Do you have an internal PKI or would you like Redwood to provision short-lived client certs?
- Expected monthly inference qps and average sequence length (tokens) so we can size the Dedicated pool if needed.

Next steps: schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff (Karthik + infra + dev) — propose Apr 20 or Apr 21. I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: networking & SDK questions — mTLS & DNS notes

Priya / Olga —

Quick technical notes from my side: 

- Client certs: Yes, we accept customer‑signed client certs (X.509 PEM). Please include the client cert CN and any app-specific SANs you depend on. We validate issuer OID and CRL/OCSP during handshake — if you can publish OCSP endpoints that's preferred.
- Rotation: If you run Vault, we recommend an automated rotation script that pushes new certs to the client store and rolls pods. Our CA integration supports short‑lived cert issuance via an API if you prefer Redwood-managed ephemeral certs.
- DNS: For private CNAME approach, create a private CNAME like api-infer.private.scarlet -> rw-infer-<region>.private.redwood.internal. TTLs of 60s are fine during rollout; we can increase post-cutover.
- SDK endpoints: Structured-output and tool-calling use the same inference endpoint and port as generation; the Content-Type and mode param differ. No additional firewall ports required.

I can drop a short example Terraform + Vault flow into the Drive folder by EOD. Also, Olga — we'll want to capture the expected qps and p50/p99 latency SLOs so we can recommend Dedicated sizing.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
